name: ackermann
axis: Ackermann — the densest call-overhead stress available: nested recursive calls in argument position, nothing memoizable or strength-reducible
notes: ack(3,10) is 44_698_325 calls to produce the number 8_189; ack(3,9) is 11_164_370. The repeat loop alternates between them via `10 - (acc & 1)` so the call is not loop-invariant — without that guard rustc hoists it. ~558M calls total. Peak recursion depth 8_190. Python is reduced to ack(3,6)/ack(3,5) (peak depth 510) because depth 8_190 is far past CPython's default limit of 1000, which is NOT raised. Scale-verified at 20 and 10 repeats (startup subtracted): rust 0.504, vl 0.513, deno 0.571 (expected 0.500). Interleaved min-of-3 on core 6: rust 0.573s, vl 1.196s, deno 2.986s, python(reduced) 4.484s. VL is 2.50x FASTER than deno and 2.09x slower than rust. This is the cleanest read on VL's NON-tail call cost, and it is healthy: `ack(m-1, ack(m, n-1))` has a genuinely non-tail inner call that no runtime can eliminate, and VL sits comfortably between rust and JS.
vlCeiling: ack(3,11) needs 16_382 frames and TRAPS in VL ('wasm trap: call stack exhausted'), while ack(3,10) at 8_190 frames succeeds — bracketing VL's measured 16_210-frame ceiling for a 2-parameter non-tail function. Deno's ceiling on the same shape is 15_625, so VL is not an outlier against its closest peer; rust reaches ~500_000.

startupBaselineSeconds._measured: min-of-10, empty program, taskset -c 6, contended 24-core i9-12900KF

compileTime._note: compile time, measured separately and never inside an execution number

consolidatedRun._method: single interleaved pass over ALL 8 recursion benchmarks, min-of-3, taskset -c 6, per-runtime empty-program startup subtracted, machine contended by other agents (loadavg ~10) so read the RATIOS not the absolutes
